Let \(A_\mu=Q_\mu\). For a quadratic \(h(x)=\frac12x^TAx\),

\[
P_{h,\rho}(v)=\rho(A+\rho I)^{-1}v.
\]

Set

\[
F=\rho(Q_\mu+\rho I)^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}a&0\\0&b\end{bmatrix},
\qquad 
G=\rho(R_\mu+\rho I)^{-1}=UFU^T,
\]

where

\[
a=\frac{\rho}{\rho+\mu},\qquad b=\frac{\rho}{\rho+4/\mu}.
\]

The relaxed DR step is linear:

\[
z^+=Mz,\qquad M=I+\theta\bigl(G(2F-I)-F\bigr).
\]

Write

\[
p=a+b,\qquad m=a-b.
\]

Using

\[
F=\frac p2I+\frac m2H,\qquad G=\frac p2I+\frac m2L,
\]

with

\[
H=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{bmatrix},\qquad
L=\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad
J=LH=\begin{bmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{bmatrix},
\]

one obtains

\[
G(2F-I)-F
=
A I+B(H+L)+D J,
\]

where

\[
A=\frac{p(p-2)}2,\qquad
B=\frac{m(p-1)}2,\qquad
D=\frac{m^2}{2}.
\]

Hence

\[
M=(1+\theta A)I+\theta B(H+L)+\theta D J.
\]

Since the operator norm is at least the root-mean-square singular value,

\[
\|M\|_2^2\ge \frac12\operatorname{tr}(M^TM)
=(1+\theta A)^2+\theta^2(2B^2+D^2).
\]

Now take the single worst-case test value \(\mu=1\). Then

\[
a=\frac{\rho}{\rho+1},\qquad b=\frac{\rho}{\rho+4},
\]

and, with \(d=(\rho+1)(\rho+4)\),

\[
p-1=\frac{\rho^2-4}{d},\qquad m=\frac{3\rho}{d}.
\]

Let

\[
\alpha=-A=\frac{p(2-p)}2,\qquad E=2B^2+D^2.
\]

Then for every \(\theta\),

\[
\|M\|_2^2\ge (1-\theta\alpha)^2+\theta^2E
\ge \frac{E}{\alpha^2+E}.
\]

A direct simplification gives

\[
81E-\alpha^2
=
\frac{\rho^2(\rho-2)^2(1358\rho^2+4612\rho+5432)}
{4(\rho+1)^4(\rho+4)^4}\ge0.
\]

Therefore

\[
\frac{E}{\alpha^2+E}\ge \frac1{82},
\]

so every admissible \((\rho,\theta)\) satisfies

\[
\mathcal C(\rho,\theta)\ge \frac1{\sqrt{82}}.
\]

Equality in the bound forces \(\rho=2\).

Now set \(\rho=2\). Then for every \(\mu\),

\[
a+b=1,
\]

so \(B=0\), \(A=-\frac12\), and

\[
M=\left(1-\frac\theta2\right)I+\theta\frac{(a-b)^2}{2}J.
\]

This is a scalar plus a skew-symmetric matrix, so

\[
\|M\|_2^2
=
\left(1-\frac\theta2\right)^2
+\theta^2\frac{(a-b)^4}{4}.
\]

Here

\[
a-b=\frac{2-\mu}{2+\mu},
\]

whose maximum absolute value on \([1,4]\) is \(1/3\). Thus

\[
\mathcal C(2,\theta)^2
=
\left(1-\frac\theta2\right)^2+\frac{\theta^2}{324}.
\]

Minimizing,

\[
\frac{d}{d\theta}
\left[
\left(1-\frac\theta2\right)^2+\frac{\theta^2}{324}
\right]
=
-1+\theta\left(\frac12+\frac1{162}\right),
\]

so

\[
\theta_*=\frac{81}{41}.
\]

At this value,

\[
\mathcal C_*^2=\frac1{82},
\qquad
\mathcal C_*=\frac1{\sqrt{82}}.
\]

Thus the unique minimizing pair is

\[
\boxed{\left(\rho_*,\theta_*,\mathcal C_*\right)
=
\left(2,\frac{81}{41},\frac1{\sqrt{82}}\right)}.
\]
